title: MCP for Unity HTTP endpoint path
question: What is the MCP for Unity HTTP endpoint path when no configurator entry exists?
fallback: Require the user to paste the URL from the MCP for Unity window
decision: Build the hub URL as <base>/mcp, default base http://127.0.0.1:8080, and take the spec fallback for discovery: the user pastes the HTTP base URL from the MCP for Unity window (doctor pre-fills the documented default and the URL of an existing configurator entry when one is there). Nothing outside the Editor's own preferences reveals a changed port.

checks.name: M1 a remote MCP URL ending in /mcp connects and lists tools
M2 every hub request goes to the /mcp path
M3 the allowed tool and the hub instructions reach the session
M4 the base URL without /mcp reaches no MCP method
M5 a wrong URL costs the session its MCP tools but not the session itself

findings: MCP for Unity stores an HTTP BASE url in EditorPrefs (default http://127.0.0.1:8080) and appends "/mcp" for the JSON-RPC endpoint; its OpenCode configurator writes { "type": "remote", "url": "<base>/mcp" } into the user's global opencode.json, and it strips a trailing "/mcp" from whatever the user types.
OpenCode 1.18.31 talks to such a URL over the streamable HTTP transport: initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list and tools/call all POST to /mcp, and a GET answered with 405 is accepted.
Pointing the same configuration at the base URL without the path yields no MCP method at all: the session still runs, but with no MCP tools, which is the failure mode doctor must name.

The port is only in the Editor's preferences, so when no configurator entry exists the user has to paste the URL from the MCP for Unity window; the live confirmation against a real hub stays a manual check.
